special education teachers leave special education primarily because of administrative factors, such as the lack of administrative support, the lack of administrative respect, and a lack of administrative recognition.
special education teachers who transfer to general education do so because of the administrative factors that they perceive as being present in special education.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the special education teacher who transfers from special education to general education does so for reasons that are related to the administrative aspects of special education and to stress factors associated with teaching special education students.
special educators who transfer out of special education do not do so because they dislike working with handicapped students.
special educators are leaving the field of special education because of a lack of support and encouragement from administrators. (Author/CL)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
teachers leave special education because they feel they have little control over the decisions made in the schools.
the majority of the special educators we studied left their special education assignment for reasons that are not unique to special education.
the most effective way to keep teachers in special education would be to improve their working conditions and to reduce the stress involved in their work. (Contains 2 tables.)
The main takeaway from our work is that
special education teachers are leaving the field for a variety of reasons, but many of these reasons are not related to their own teaching performance.
the special education system should be more flexible and supportive of teachers' needs and desires.
special education teachers who leave special education are likely to remain in education and may be good candidates for general education teaching assignments.
